Issued at 552 AM EDT Sat Sep 12 2026

A warm front near Indy as of this writing will continue to lift 
northeastward through the day, reaching our area later this morning 
around 12-15z, then heading into Southern Ontario/Lake Erie by 
around 18z. Warm air/moisture advection is forcing an area of rain 
and thunderstorms near the front, and this will lift into our area 
for the morning. Was initially suspicious the thunder would not make 
it here, but as of 9z it looks fairly healthy thanks to some 
elevated instability. As the warm front moves north, moisture 
transport takes on a more east-northeasterly track-so have the best 
chances along and south of US 24 (best east of I 69) through the 
morning/early afternoon. Meanwhile, an upper level trough/shortwave 
and surface cold front approaches from the west. As of this writing, 
the boundary extends southward from western Lake Superior into West-
Central WI/Eastern MN and IA/IL. Models don't seem to have a great 
handle on the precipitation associated with this feature (many are 
dry at this time in the latest runs). Its fairly light, but there 
are a couple thunderstorms near the IL/WI line. The actual upper 
level trough and surface front look to reach our western CWA border 
by 00z (right along Lake MI shore, extending from IL into northern 
Ontario). Some of the models indicate a pre-frontal trough possibly 
developing towards the afternoon, which could re-invigorate the 
already moistened atmosphere in areas mainly along/south of US 24. I 
suspect as the better moisture transport gradually diminishes and 
shifts more E-NE out of our area late this morning that we'll see a 
diminishing trend to the precipitation along the incoming cold front 
(thus keeping areas further north and west of US 24 dry with 
variable cloud cover). In the afternoon, the shortwave/pre-frontal 
trough is likely to trip an increase in shower/storm activity again, 
especially as it arrives at a time of decent heating (sfc cape 
potentially up to 1500 J/kg). Luckily we don't have much in the way 
of any shear or steep mid level lapse rates, so not expecting any 
severe weather at this time. 

Otherwise, heating up into the mid-upper 80s for many locations 
today (especially further northwest where cloud cover is lower/no 
precipitation). Expect dry conditions tonight as the cold front 
moves through, with winds shifting west-northwest. While winds 
overnight are lower initially, they increase out of the N-NW Sunday 
morning into the afternoon, especially near Lake MI and along/north 
of the toll road. If winds on Lake MI increase to 15kts sustained 
and gust to around 20-25 knots...we could end up seeing waves of 3-5 
feet on Lake MI. However, the past few runs of models have flip 
flopped on the intensity of these winds (initially lighter with 2-3 
ft waves). Opted to hold off on the beach hazards statement this 
issuance, but did maintain a high swim risk forecast for both La 
Porte/Berrien County beaches. If stronger winds verify, waves should 
reach 3-5 feet fairly quickly, approaching at angles of 45 to 90 
degrees relative to shore with 6-7 second periods. This would be 
ideal for strong rip and structural currents, and a strong southward 
flowing longshore current. If heading to Lake MI this weekend, make 
plans for out of the water activities. I suspect the confidence for 
this forecast will be higher by this afternoon. 

Rain and storms are possible again on Sunday afternoon/evening as 
another trough swings through and the cold front potentially gets 
hung up to our south and another weak trough moves in before high 
pressure builds in from the northwest. Have chances (20-30%) mainly 
west of IN-15, then east of IN 15 chances focus further south of US 
30 where the front could get hung up. Highs Sunday will be in the 
mid-upper 70s, low 80s. 

Monday will be cooler and dry, with highs in the 70s. Sfc high 
pressure/an upper level ridge builds into the Great Lakes briefly, 
then by Mon night into Tue the surface high drifts east and the 
upper level ridge takes on a SW to NE orientation (extending into 
the lower Great Lakes and the NE CONUS). We'll be on the periphery 
of this ridge, and as an upper low/surface low move through Ontario, 
it brings a trough and cold front eastward into our forecast area. 
There is uncertainty as to whether the precipitation chances arrive 
Monday night or closer to Tuesday afternoon. Either way, expect the 
front and precipitation/storm chances to cross from west to east 
through late Mon PM into Tuesday. However, the front does appear to 
stall out as it is limited by subsidence from the staunch upper 
ridge still lingering. This would result in a boundary over our 
forecast area that may linger into Thursday or Friday. For now, have 
20-50% chances Tuesday (mainly north/west of US 24), then increasing 
to 30-70% by Tuesday night into Thursday (40-60%). There will be
